So the reason I got this is fairly simple.

I'm 40 next year, and my dentist tells me every 6 months I need to floss, I hate flossing. I hate it because its uncomfortable, my teeth are close and I just hate it. I'm like a stubborn 6yo. Soooo I won't floss.

Secondly, I just fot a new (expensive) electric toothbrush from my partner, and after 5 weeks, the rubber on it started to peel. what a joke.

But even more the actual vibrating on it felt generic and simple, nothing new under the sun.

So my proposed solution last week, was buy expensive water based flosser, and go for the top of the line Braun or Oral-b electric ultrasonic toothbrush. And just live with a massive tech park on my vanity.

Then because I suck at ordering things online, I simply procrastinated long enough for this week to happen, and for Dyson to somehow reinvent the electric toothbrush just in time for me to not have to install a dentist tech park in my bathroom.

I'm I stoked about a live video feed of the inside of my gums? Hell yeah, I'm I scared to death about the micro explosions that will happen in my mouth every time I brush me teeth... yes absofuckinglutely.

But as a nerd, and early tech lover, I could not sit this one out, I had to get it, but I hovered on the order site, decided to make lunch, and once I returned it was sold out, EVERYWHERE.

But as luck has it, there is a flagship store, and since most people these days hate going to the store, I went there. BUT it was sold out, except they had just gotten a new shipment, and now I have one.

I'll give me feedback tomorrow, on initial experience, but expect a longer in-depth breakdown a few weeks from now.

I want to love it, but I'm not sure that will be the case.

quotedPost.text:
What if a dexterous robot could learn a 20+ step chemistry experiment without a single on-robot training demo?

Meet TwinDEX: a pair of co-designed, three-finger, nine-DoF dexterous manipulation interface: one wearable for data collection, one for robot deployment.

The twinned design shares identical kinematics, contact surfaces, visual appearance, and sensors across collection and deployment — keeping observations and actions aligned end to end.

Trained from scratch on only a few hundred wearable demonstrations - with zero on-robot training or intervention data - TwinDEX completed a standardized chemistry experiment involving tool switches, fine force control, and bimanual coordination.

Robot-free data showed comparable learning efficiency on the multi-task evaluation, TwinDEX delivered 5.3 times effective throughput than on-robot teleoperation.

TwinDEX demonstrates that high-quality robot-free data can fully substitute for on-robot teleoperation data on challenging dexterous tasks — removing the dependency on real-robot hardware that has been the central bottleneck to scaling dexterous manipulation data.

This was the proof-it phase. Now comes scale: what emerges at tens of thousands, or millions, of episodes?

Watch the demo and read the technical blog: https://t.co/PgyFkrJdXG

#TwinDEX #Robotics #EmbodiedAI #DexterousManipulation

In 2025 a startup paid $12M for https://t.co/VHvFHp5ZgW and launched as "The First AI Admaker."

A year later it relaunched as:
"The Human Admaker"

Icon had everything an AI startup is supposed to have. A seed led by Founders Fund. Backers from OpenAI, Google, even Saquon Barkley. A pitch that sounded inevitable: paste a URL, get UGC ads generated at scale.

Then mid-2025 the site went dark. People wrote the obituary.

The comeback is interesting. They looked at what actually converts and rebuilt around real creators. Thats a Pivot.

The math checks out:

AI UGC: $1 per video. 1 in 87 converts. $87 per winning asset.
Human UGC: $15 per video. 1 in 4 converts. $60 per winning asset.

The cheap option is the expensive one.

The market explains it. There are 30+ AI UGC tools right now. Arcads, Creatify, HeyGen, a new one every week. All the same workflow: paste a link, pick an avatar, export 50 variations. Feeds are flooded with it and people scroll straight past.

AI can fake a face.
It can't fake being trusted.

So the new Icon puts humans in front of the camera. They find the creators,  write the scripts, coach the shoot, film, edit.
6 finished ads for $999.

Icon-made ads have passed 1B views across Meta, TikTok and YouTube.

Instead of trying to have AI run your ads business, you are now in charge instead.

China is adding a Germany sized grid in 2025. 
Made up almost entirely from wind and solar. 

If we look at overall energy production, China has been accelerating since 2000. 

The US is now starting to bend the curve, and if they could match China, it would still take them 25 years to catch up. 

Energy dominance will be the determining factor for the future. If we look at per capita use tho the US is still in the lead, but that could also be a sign of waste as seen in the 3rd chart. 

My thesis is that countries like Switzerland, Ireland, Austria, Sweden etc are showing where we are headed. 

It's not just about wasteful energy use, it's about smart use. When you upgrade your entire country to be more energy efficient, you can reap the benefits of lower overall per capita use and still lead over someone thats wasting energy. 

We can see clearly that Ireland has higher GDP than the US, while using only 27.000 kilowatt per person a year, compared to the US at a whopping 75.000 per person a year. 

While I still argue the ultimate measure of a countries success will be its energy output per capita. I do believe at the same time we might need a better way to meassure this, and GDP won't cut it.

the taurus brain be like this 24/7, people would be genuinely shocked, because everyone assumes it’s peaceful in there.

It isn’t. It’s a room stacked with every purchase they’re evaluating, every person’s behaviour they’ve been quietly assessing for months.

I know. I’m a taurus. this is the way.

a mental inventory of everything I own, and a very detailed plan for a life I haven’t told anyone about yet.

What people misunderstand about Taurus is that calm on the outside doesn’t mean quiet on the inside.

we’re constantly evaluating, comfort, cost, value, whether that person is trustworthy, whether this decision is worth it, whether they should say something.

The processing takes forever. literally. we never finish anything. or if we do, it’s probably after months of procrastination.

A Taurus will spend weeks turning something over before reaching a conclusion, which is why their decisions look sudden from the outside but were actually finalized ages ago in complete privacy. much to my partners demise.

What makes it exhausting is the pressure to appear unbothered. when in reality we’re pretty bothered.

Everyone relies on the Taurus being the steady one, so the internal calculations stay entirely hidden. because if I break. then the whole system comes crashing down on itself. me.

So if a Taurus (me) seems slow to respond or oddly quiet, they’re (I’m) not disengaged.

They’re just running the whole thing internally, while constantly building enough context window that we could survive an apocalypse.

It’s not you, it’s me.

the sound of an ambulance is loud 
until it’s coming to your home 

a crying baby on an airplane is irritating
until you learn you can’t have one
